### AM-058: self-contained version metadata (owner-approved)

The bundle carries no application `package.json`. The packaging script reads
`server/package.json` as the version source and injects its JSON-encoded string
with esbuild `--define:__APUNTA_VERSION__`. Both application version readers
use that constant when defined and retain their existing relative
`createRequire` reads as lazy source-execution fallbacks otherwise. Preserve
source/tsx/dist/Node type-stripping execution and the existing English version
semantics. Do not use blind source replacement or place metadata outside the
bundle. **Verify that these two runtime version reads no longer carry their package
metadata into the bundle, by a fingerprint that can actually fail** (independent review D1: the value assertion
alone cannot discriminate, because `server/package.json`'s version is `0.0.0` and
both readers fall back to that same literal, and because an esbuild that inlines
the read as an object literal travels with the bundle and takes the path strings
with it, so a path grep passes while the metadata still ships). So the check is:

- **Source shape, required.** The define guard must be
  `typeof __APUNTA_VERSION__ === 'string'`, never a bare reference — `declare
  const` is erased by type stripping, and a bare reference throws
  `ReferenceError` in exactly the raw type-stripped case named above.
- **What the greps do and do not prove, stated exactly.** They prove the
  package metadata is **not inlined** into the bundle, which is the failure the
  card cares about: an inlined read travels with the bundle, and a relocated
  read is what produced the original defect. They do **not** prove the word
  "eliminated" in the strongest sense — `config.ts`'s `createRequire` is a local
  binding, so esbuild leaves `require('../package.json')` unresolved and the JSON
  is never inlined even though the read is still textually present. That
  survivor is unobservable in every row here, because the required `typeof`
  guard makes the defined path the only one that can execute. Stating it
  plainly is better than letting the row's name imply more than it checks.
- **Bundle shape, required, and now falsifiable.** Two greps over
  `build/linux-resources/server/server.mjs`, each of which must be `0`:
  - `grep -c '__APUNTA_VERSION__'` — esbuild substitutes the define, so any
    surviving occurrence means the define was not applied on that path. No
    dependency uses this name, so the count is attributable.
  - `grep -c '@apunta/server'` — the `name` field of the `package.json` both
    readers resolve, which esbuild drags in whole whenever it inlines that file.
    Both
    readers require **relative** paths, so a self-resolving name is exactly the
    failure; the string appears in zero files under `server/src` or `shared/src`
    today.
  A non-zero count on either is `FAIL`. These two are the whole check;
  unrelated dependency metadata strings are not a failure.

  **Correction, and the reason this text exists at all:** the first attempt at
  this fingerprint counted `createRequire`, on the reasoning that it occurs in
  exactly two hand-written files. That is true of the repository and false of
  the **bundle**, which inlines `node_modules`: `fflate`'s Node ESM entry calls
  `createRequire` at module scope, is unconditionally live, and is reached from
  the server's own entry. The count could never be `0`, so the check could never
  pass and would have blocked a correct implementation. A fingerprint has to be
  checked against the artefact it will be run on, not against the source tree it
  came from.

The packaging test must assert both health's `version` and the sandbox lock's
`appVersion` equal the version read from `server/package.json`, including after
relocation. Run associated source regression tests plus lint/typecheck on the
stable implementation tree. Keep the original missing-SQLite failure assertions.
Stop only the first owned PID and establish the port is free before launching
the broken copy; preserve C-ISO ownership verification for that launch too.
**The rule-5 ownership proof, resolved (independent review D2).** The
boot-error app hard-codes its health response and cannot carry `testRunId`
without an edit outside May edit, and `boot-error.ts` is not editable — so the
poll-based proof is unavailable for the broken-copy launch. **No waiver is
needed, because a stronger proof exists and it is the one C-OWN@1 already uses:**
prove ownership from the data-folder lock file the process itself writes.
Assert, while the process is **alive** (a clean release unlinks it, so a
post-mortem read is not a proof of anything):

1. `acquireDataFolderLock` precedes `openDatabase`, which precedes serving the
   boot error, so by the time `/api/health` answers the lock is already written
   by that process — there is no race to lose.
2. On `$APUNTA_DATA_DIR/apunta.lock`: `pid` equals the spawned pid;
   `processStart` equals field 22 of `/proc/<pid>/stat` for that same live pid
   (what the production helper computes); that pid is alive; and the port was
   bound-and-released free immediately before launch.
3. The folder is the wrapper's own `0700` run directory, so no foreign process
   can have written our pid's kernel start time into it.

This catches every failure mode rule 5 exists for — a pre-existing dummy on the
port, a lost race, pid reuse, a stale lock, a healthy server left running —
because it compares a kernel identity rather than an environment echo, and a
stale lock needs no instruction: taking over replaces a dead owner's file and a
clean exit unlinks it. **The missing-SQLite assertions are kept and this proof is
added to them**; the `appVersion` assertion reads from the same live lock file.

**One residual, named rather than papered over (independent review).** The lock
proves that *our process* owns the data folder. It does not, by itself, prove
that the process answering HTTP is that same process: a third party that bound
the port in the window between our free-port check and our `listen` would satisfy
every lock assertion. So the card requires one further assertion at the moment
the server answers: **the listening socket on the test port must be owned by the
spawned pid** (read the socket's owning pid from `/proc/net/tcp` matched against
`/proc/<pid>/fd`, or `ss -ltnp` under the bundled environment). With that, the
proof covers both halves — the responder is our process, and our process holds
the lock. Without it, do not claim the proof is equivalent to `testRunId`.
Mac build-time version alignment is carried to P6.1, not edited by this card.

## Steps
1. Write the test first, and run it through `sandbox.mjs` in **`env` mode**,
   never `run` mode. `run` spawns `join(repoRoot, 'server', 'dist', 'index.js')`
   with `process.execPath` and `cwd: repoRoot` (`sandbox.mjs:50,258-268`) and
   refuses outright when that entry is missing, so it would start the **repo's**
   server under whatever Node ran the wrapper — never the bundled one — and the
   run would pass without proving the objective. The test therefore:
   `<folder>/node/bin/node <abs-repo>/scripts/v2/sandbox.mjs env --port 7845`
   (the wrapper is a Node script in the checkout, so it is named by absolute
   path and run with the bundled Node rather than found on `PATH`; `<p>` is
   `--port` from the dispatch), then source the seven `export` lines it prints;
   copy the whole output to `/tmp/apunta-v2/${APUNTA_TEST_RUN_ID}/bundle/`;
   `cd /`; and start `<folder>/node/bin/node <folder>/server/server.mjs` itself,
   with the launch contract above plus the wrapper's `APUNTA_DATA_DIR` and
   `APUNTA_PORT`, and a `PATH` holding no host Node at all (`/usr/bin:/bin` —
   the box's default `node` is a mise shim, v26.8.2).
2. **The rule-5 ownership check is the test's own here**, because `env` mode
   only creates the run folder and prints the exports (`sandbox.mjs:353-361`) —
   it performs no poll. Before any assertion the test polls `/api/health` for up
   to 30 s and proceeds only when `testRunId` equals `$APUNTA_TEST_RUN_ID`;
   silence, a missing id or a foreign id fails the run. On exit, including on
   failure, it stops only the PID it started (never `pkill`, C-ISO@1 rule 7) and
   asserts that nothing is still listening on `<p>`.
3. The checks, each printing `PASS <name>` or `FAIL <name>: <detail>`, the
   script exiting non-zero on the first failure:
   - **health** — `GET /api/health` is 200, `ok` is `true`, and `testRunId` is
     this run's.
   - **migration on a fresh database** — `db.path` from that response is under
     `$APUNTA_DATA_DIR`, and `db.migrationLevel` equals the highest version
     among the `.sql` files in the bundled `migrations/` (all of them applied
     on an empty database).
   - **note creation needs a patient and a format first**: `POST
     /api/patients`; `POST /api/formats` with the route's own required body
     (a fresh database has **zero** formats,
     so `GET /api/formats` returns an empty list and the note call cannot be
     made otherwise); then `POST /api/notes` with that `format_id` →
     `GET /api/notes/<id>` returns the same id. On a fresh data dir `POST
     /api/notes` alone is `404 not_found` (`notes.ts:47-53` calls
     `requirePatient`, which throws `notFound('Patient not found')` →
     `server/src/http/errors.ts:85-87`; there is no `patient_not_found` code).
   - **the shipped SPA** — `GET /` is 200 with `content-type: text/html` and a
     non-empty body, read from the bundled `web/dist` through
     `APUNTA_WEB_DIST`; an empty or truncated copy of `web/dist` must fail here
     rather than in a person's browser.
   - **the whisper binary** — `<folder>/bin/whisper-cli --help` exits 0, so the
     copied shared libraries resolve next to it.
   - **the failure case** — in the copied folder, rename
     `native/better_sqlite3.node` and start the bundled server again:
     `server/src/index.ts:27-80` catches the `openDatabase` failure, serves the
     boot-error page and **keeps the port bound**, so the process does **not**
     exit. The test asserts the boot-error behaviour instead — `GET /` is the
     boot-error page and `/api/health` answers `503` with `storage_error` — and
     then kills the process it started. A server that starts normally and answers
     health `200` is `FAIL`; the test's own exit code stays 0 because the broken
     copy really did fail to open the database.
4. Implement until it passes.

A non-zero count is `FAIL`, and so is a run that cannot execute because the bundle is missing: that is `NOT RUN`, not a pass. This row exists because the fingerprint was previously stated in prose with no row behind it, leaving an implementation reviewer nothing to re-run |
| V3 | `export PATH="$HOME/.local/share/apunta-node/node-v24.19.0-linux-x64/bin:$PATH" && node -e "const m=require('./build/linux-resources/manifest.json');process.exit(m.files.length>0?0:1)"` | exit 0. `files` is the array Fixed decisions fixes, each entry `{path, bytes, sha256}` with `path` relative to the folder — a manifest shaped `{"files": {"node/bin/node": "…"}}` evaluates `undefined > 0` and exits 1, which is the point of fixing the shape. `compiler` and `glibc` are recorded, and every path V1 lists is present with its SHA-256; the manifest path set equals all bundled files except manifest.json, with actual byte counts and hashes verified |

## Stop conditions
- **`cmake` or the compiler the chosen backend needs is missing** (`hipcc` for
  `hip`, `glslc` for `vulkan`): report which tool, and mark the build rows
  `BLOCKED` — `scripts/build-whisper-candidate.sh` exits 2 before it builds
  anything. Agents never install a tool (HS-3); the card stays `BLOCKED` until
  the owner resolves it. Do not substitute a different toolchain to get a green
  row.
  **This condition was false as written and has been corrected (independent
  review F2, the earlier D5).** It asserted that the build tool this backend
  needs was missing on this PC. That was not true: the owner installed `cmake`
  on 2026-09-26 and 4.4.3 is at
  `/usr/bin/cmake`, with `glslc` 2026.3 present, so the `vulkan` backend is
  buildable and `hipcc` is the one genuinely absent tool. An implementer reading
  the old text would have filed `BLOCKED` for a tool that is installed, on the
  card's own instruction. Check the tool before reporting anything.
- The A06 clone cannot reach `github.com`: report. Do not substitute a mirror,
  and do not adopt a `whisper-cli` found elsewhere on the machine without
  recording it under `ACQUISITION.md` §2 "already present" with its version.
- `node_modules/better-sqlite3/prebuilds/linux-x64.node` is absent, or does not
  load under the bundled Node 24.19.0: report the loader's own error. Do **not**
  compile it, do not run `deps/download.sh`, and do not fall back to the host's
  `build/Release` copy — the copy step is the fix, not a build.

# Contract excerpts (authoritative)

## C-ISO@1 Isolation and the sandbox wrapper

**Built by** P0.3. **Proven by** P0.3 (negative tests) and Q1.1.
**Consumers:** every card that starts a server, opens a real database, runs
e2e, runs `check:format`/`check:refine`, runs a real-model eval or launches
the app.

**Interface** (`scripts/v2/sandbox.mjs`, Node, no dependencies):

| Command | Behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| `node scripts/v2/sandbox.mjs run --port <p> -- <cmd...>` | Creates run folder, starts server, verifies ownership, runs `<cmd>` with the sandbox environment, stops only what it started, exits with `<cmd>`'s code |
| `node scripts/v2/sandbox.mjs env --port <p>` | Creates run folder only, prints `export` lines for tools that start their own server (Playwright) |
| `node scripts/v2/sandbox.mjs selftest` | Runs the negative cases below; exit 0 only if all refuse correctly |

**Rules**
1. Run folder: `/tmp/apunta-v2/<runId>/` with `data/`, `logs/`, `tmp/`,
   mode `700`. `runId` = UTC timestamp + 8 random hex characters.
   `realpath` of every path must stay under `/tmp/apunta-v2/`; a symlink that
   escapes is refused.
2. Port must be an integer 7800 to 7889 and free (checked by binding, then
   released immediately before the server binds). 7717 is always refused.
   7890 to 7899 are reserved for the updater test server (C-UPD) and refused
   here.
3. The data folder is never the platform default. The wrapper computes the
   default with `platformDataDir()` (C-PATH) **as a string only** and refuses
   if the sandbox path equals it or is inside it. It never lists or opens the
   default.
4. Server environment: `APUNTA_DATA_DIR`, `APUNTA_PORT`, `APUNTA_NO_OPEN=1`,
   `APUNTA_TEST_RUN_ID=<runId>`, `APUNTA_V2=1`. When `APUNTA_TEST_RUN_ID` is
   set, `/api/health` includes `"testRunId"`; the field never appears
   otherwise.
5. Ownership check: the wrapper polls `/api/health` for up to 30 s and
   proceeds only if `testRunId` equals its `runId`. Anything else (no
   answer, a different id, no id) is refused and the child is stopped.
6. Child command environment adds `APUNTA_CHECK_URL`, `APUNTA_E2E_PORT`,
   `APUNTA_V2=1`.
7. Cleanup kills only the process group the wrapper created. Never `pkill`,
   never the Ollama daemon.
8. When `APUNTA_V2=1`: Playwright sets `reuseExistingServer: false`;
   `scripts/check-note-format.mjs` and `scripts/check-refine.mjs` exit 2 if
   `APUNTA_CHECK_URL` is unset or points at port 7717.

**Normal example.** `sandbox.mjs run --port 7801 -- npm run check:format`
→ run folder created, server answers with the matching `testRunId`, the
check runs against `http://127.0.0.1:7801`, server stopped, exit code of the
check.

**Rejection examples** (each must be a `selftest` case, refused before any
database is opened): `--port 7717`; `--port 7890`; port in use by a dummy
listener; a dummy server on the port answering `/api/health` with 200 but no
or wrong `testRunId`; run folder symlinked outside `/tmp/apunta-v2/`;
`APUNTA_DATA_DIR` equal to the platform default string.

# Run configuration (v2 plan)

## 1. Ports

| Use | Port |
| --- | --- |
| Live instance: **never contact** | 7717 |
| Sandbox servers (C-ISO) | 7800 to 7889 |
| Updater test server (C-UPD) | 7890 to 7899 |
| Playwright under the sandbox | the port `sandbox.mjs env` assigns |

## 2. Gate levels

A card names one level. Commands run from the repository root unless a card
says otherwise. Until P0.3 is APPROVED, only L0 and the non-launching part of
L1 may run.

| Level | When | Commands |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **L0** docs only | cards that change only Markdown | `npx prettier --check <changed files>`; `node scripts/check-no-external-urls.mjs` |
| **L1** targeted | every implementation card | `npm run lint`; `npm run typecheck`; `npm run build:shared`, then the card's named test files with `npx vitest run <paths>` from the repository root (the root `vitest.config.ts` defines the projects) |
| **L2** parent acceptance | every parent review card | everything in §3 |
| **L3** native or real model | cards and parent reviews that say so | the card's listed commands, all through `sandbox.mjs` |

## 3. The L2 suite

```sh
npm run lint
npm run typecheck
TZ=UTC npm test
TZ=America/Denver npm test
TZ=America/Mexico_City npm test
TZ=Australia/Sydney npm test
npm run build
node scripts/v2/sandbox.mjs env --port 7810 > /tmp/apunta-v2-e2e.env && . /tmp/apunta-v2-e2e.env && npm run e2e
npm run eval -- --fake --runs 1
```

After P0.2, each `TZ=` run prints its effective zone (a test asserts it), so
four runs really exercise four zones. After P0.3, the e2e line is the only
permitted way to run Playwright. After S3.2, add
`npm run eval -- --fake --runs 1 --corpus e2e/fixtures/eval-es/tuning`.
After P3.3, add `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` and
`cargo test` in `src-tauri/`.

## 4. Evidence

- Write detailed output to `docs/v2/evidence/<card-id>/`. Keep it sanitized:
  replace sandbox paths with `<sandbox>`, the home folder with `~`, and never
  include hostnames, usernames, keys, tokens or real names.
- Raw logs stay in the sandbox run folder and are never committed.
- Each command's evidence records: working directory, exact command, exit
  code, start and end time, and a short excerpt (failures in full, up to 200
  lines).
- Status words: criteria `NOT RUN`, `PASS`, `FAIL`, `BLOCKED`; cards
  `NOT STARTED`, `IN PROGRESS`, `SUBMITTED`, `APPROVED`,
  `CHANGES REQUESTED`, `BLOCKED`; instruction reviews `CLEAR`, `DEFECT`,
  `UNKNOWN`. Every blank template starts at `NOT RUN` or `UNKNOWN`.

**Redirect admission (rule 1).** A redirect is followed only when its `Location`
resolves to `https:`, port 443, no user-info, no fragment, a host the row's
*Redirect hosts* cell admits, and a query whose every parameter name appears in
that row's *Allowed query keys* cell. A parameter name outside the cell is
refused (`query_key_not_allowed`) before the URL is requested. `none` means the
row admits no query at all, so any query is `query_not_allowed` — that is the
default and it is unchanged. No row admits a query by wildcard, a prefix or a
blanket permission, and the cell is the complete list: adding a name is a
plan-editor amendment (AM-042).

**Why A07's names are safe to enumerate.** The ten names are the AWS
CloudFront signed-URL parameter set plus Hugging Face's Xet and
`response-content-*` parameters, observed on 2026-09-26 across all six C-STT
artifacts and the one speech artifact, each answering `302` to
`us.aws.cdn.hf.co` (`docs/v2/evidence/P4.1/redirects.md`). They cannot change
*which* bytes arrive: the path is fixed by the pinned catalogue URL and the
bytes are verified against the pinned `sha256`, and the committed name is the
entry's own `sizeBytes` path, so the two `response-content-*` parameters can
only shape headers a client would have sent anyway. The card's own worry — "a
query string is where a download URL turns into a message" — is about
*outbound* data, and none of these names carries any: the probe records the
**names** only and writes every value as `<redacted>`, so a signature is never
in the repository, the evidence or any log.

**The four-arm comparison (A13, A14, A15).** Added 2026-09-26 on the owner's
approval, for one measurement round and nothing else. The arms are
`qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M` as the control (A08; already present, and A08's "never pulled
if present" still holds), plus A13, A14 and A15. Three rules bind the round and
are not negotiable per run:

1. **No candidate becomes a default.** A07's "selected one only" and A08's tag
   are unchanged. The round measures; it does not promote.
2. **The licence of A14 and A15 is unknown to the coordinator and must be found
   before either is pulled.** These are models downloaded by the user at setup,
   so L-POLICY@1's row for that applies: per the publisher's licence, shown and
   recorded. Prism's licence for these repositories is not asserted here because
   it was not verified — anyone pulling them records the licence text and the
   URL it came from, or reports `BLOCKED`. Guessing it is exactly the failure
   this manifest exists to prevent.
3. **The GPU is not shared.** One model loaded at a time, `keep_alive` set so
   each unloads after its arm, and no arm runs while the owner is testing on the
   machine or a live instance is in use. A four-arm run is long and real.

**Fraunces (A16) follows Kalam, not a build-time download.** Both source TTFs live in `docs/v2/assets/` with their OFL texts, and `build-brand-fraunces.py` reads the local file and touches no network — regenerating the wordmark in six years must not depend on a `/tmp` file or a download working. A16 permits exactly that one fetch, to obtain the file committed beside it. Fraunces is a **variable** font; the committed cut is the variable one, and the generator pins `wght 500`, `opsz 14`, `SOFT 0`, `WONK 0`, because a static instance could not set optical size and an unpinned variable font would not reproduce. The TTF is never bundled: the app ships outlines only.

**Owner-run items.** `apt` needs `sudo`. The coordinator writes the exact
command to `docs/v2/state/OWNER-ACTIONS.md`, stops the dependent cards, and
waits; the owner runs it. Agents never enter a password.

**Ollama.** Before any pull, run `ollama list`; if the tag exists, do not pull.
Record the digest with `ollama show <tag>`. Real-model runs set Ollama's
`keep_alive` so evaluation models unload after use, and run only one model
at a time, to avoid starving the live instance.

## 2. Development tools already present

Anything already installed on the PC (git, Python, Piper if present,
whisper-cli, Ollama) may be used as found. Record its version in evidence.

## 3. L-POLICY@1 Licences

One rule, applied per object reviewed (a tool, a library, a model file, a
voice, a dictionary, generated audio are separate objects).

| Object | Allowed |
| --- | --- |
| Code or data **shipped** in the app or installer | MIT, BSD, Apache-2.0, ISC, Zlib, 0BSD, Unicode, OFL-1.1 (fonts), CC0, CC-BY-4.0 (data, with attribution) |
| The one pre-approved exception | Spanish dictionary **data** under an MPL option of a multi-licence, shipped unmodified in its own files, election and obligations stated in `THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES.md` and `docs/decisions.md` |
| Development-only tools never shipped or linked | any OSI licence, including GPL (Piper) |
| Generated fixtures committed to the repo | only if the voice's model card permits redistribution of generated audio; otherwise generate at test time into the sandbox and never commit |
| Models downloaded by the user at setup | per the publisher's licence, shown in setup, recorded in the catalogue |
| System libraries bundled into an AppImage (for example WebKitGTK, LGPL) | allowed for **test builds**; **public distribution requires owner review** (listed in the final report) |

Anything else: do not add it; the card reports `BLOCKED` with the licence
text found. A dependency's MIT wrapper does not change its data's licence.
